'''Jason Rosenhouse''' is an American author and professor of mathematics at [[James Madison University]]. His research focuses on [[algebraic graph theory]], as well as [[analytic number theory]].<ref name=CV>{{Cite web|url=http://educ.jmu.edu/~rosenhjd/rosenhouseCV2.pdf|title=Jason Rosenhouse Curriculum Vitae}}</ref> He ran the '''Evolution Blog''' at [[National Geographic (magazine)|National Geographic]]'s [[ScienceBlogs]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://scienceblogs.com/evolutionblog/ |title=EvolutionBlog - Science, Religion, Math, Politics and Chess |publisher=Scienceblogs.com |access-date=2013-10-27}}</ref> where he was a frequent critic of [[creationism]],<ref>{{cite web|author=jrosenhouse on July 9, 2013 |url=http://scienceblogs.com/evolutionblog/2013/07/09/creationists-loves-them-some-thermodynamics/ |title=Creationists Loves Them Some Thermodynamics! – EvolutionBlog |publisher=Scienceblogs.com |date=2013-07-09 |access-date=2013-10-27}}</ref> he has contributed to the pro-evolution blog ''[[The Panda's Thumb (blog)|The Panda's Thumb]]'',<ref>{{cite web | url=http://pandasthumb.org/archives/author/jason-rosenhouse/ | title=Jason Rosenhouse Archives | work=The Panda's Thumb Blog | access-date=31 January 2014 | author=Rosenhouse, Jason | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140204000501/http://pandasthumb.org/archives/author/jason-rosenhouse/ | archive-date=4 February 2014 | url-status=dead }}</ref> and he has written for the ''[[HuffPost]]'' on topics such as the [[Higgs boson]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.huffingtonpost.com/jason-rosenhouse/faith-in-the-higgs_b_1828182.html | title=Faith in the Higgs? | work=[[Huffington Post]] | date=30 August 2012 | access-date=27 October 2013 | author=Rosenhouse, Jason}}</ref> He is also the author and editor of several books on [[recreational mathematics]].

==Personal life==
Jason grew up in New Jersey. While in middle school and high school, he was a prolific chess player, attending both tournaments and chess camp.<ref>[https://chess-db.com/public/pinfo.jsp?id=2039818 Unknown]{{Dead link|date=October 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://ratings.fide.com/|title=FIDE Ratings Database. Rankings and Search.|website=International Chess Federation (FIDE)}}</ref>

==Education==
Rosenhouse has a bachelor's degree from [[Brown University]] in mathematics (1995), and an M.A. (1997) and PhD in mathematics (2000), both from [[Dartmouth College]].<ref name=CV/> His PhD thesis was entitled "Isoperimetric numbers of certain Cayley graphs associated to PSL (2, [zeta subscript n])".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://search.worldcat.org/title/80403035|title=Isoperimetric numbers of certain Cayley graphs associated to PSL (2, [zeta subscript n]) &#124; WorldCat.org|website=search.worldcat.org}}</ref>

==Career==
In 2000, Rosenhouse accepted a position at [[Kansas State University]]'s mathematics department, at a time when the state school board was embroiled in a dispute over teaching creationism in schools. The school board's elimination of evolution from science textbooks introduced him to the creationist community, and he says that his time spent with them has convinced him that "the task of reconciling science with faith is far more difficult than is sometimes pretended."<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.huffingtonpost.com/jason-rosenhouse/atheist-learns-from-creationists_b_1343147.html | title=What One Atheist Learned From Hanging Out With Creationists | work=[[Huffington Post]] | date=21 March 2012 | access-date=27 October 2013 | author=Rosenhouse, Jason}}</ref>
He was appointed assistant professor at [[James Madison University]] in 2003 and full professor in 2014.
